claim: Isarithmic (contour-style) maps yield better understanding of hazard-exposure uncertainty than gradational shaded or binned maps.
stance_target: evidence-based map design improves hazard comprehension
quoted_support: isarithmic maps produce the better understanding of uncertainty about hazard exposure than gradational shaded or binned maps (Thompson et al., 2015 ; Mulder et al., 2017 ).

claim: Hazard-map research has focused on correcting erroneous inferences but neglected displays that support timely protective-action decisions.
stance_target: evidence-based map design improves hazard comprehension
quoted_support: it has neglected the development and testing of spatial displays that can help people to make more timely and effective protective action decisions.

claim: People's risk judgments follow a proximity heuristic: perceived risk decreases monotonically with distance from the hazard source.
stance_target: evidence-based map design improves hazard comprehension
quoted_support: people's risk judgments can be characterized by a proximity heuristic (Teigen, 2005 ), which generates a perceived risk gradient that is a monotone decreasing function of distance from a hazard source
